# Automating Kanzi Studio tasks[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#automating-ks-tasks "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
You can execute Kanzi Studio commands by running a script from the command line interface. This enables you to automate repetitive tasks in Kanzi Studio or Kanzi Studio tasks that you must execute on a large number of Kanzi Studio projects. For example, consider making a script to update a Kanzi Engine plugin that you use in many Kanzi Studio projects, or to export kzb files from many Kanzi Studio projects.
For the list of available commands, see [Kanzi Studio command reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html).
To automate Kanzi Studio tasks:
  1. In a text editor, create a script where you define what commands you want Kanzi Studio to run.
For example, add to the script the commands in this step and save the script as `MyScript.txt`.
    1. Open a Kanzi Studio project.

```
# Open the project named MyProject.
LoadProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyProject\Tool_project\MyProject.proj.kzm"

```
Copy to clipboard
    2. Add commands to automate Kanzi Studio tasks.
For example, you can automate:
       * Exporting of kzb files. See [Exporting kzb files using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#exporting-kzb-files-using-a-script).
       * Building of Kanzi applications for Android. See [Building Kanzi applications for Android using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#building-kanzi-applications-for-android-using-script).
       * Importing and updating of Kanzi Engine plugins. See [Importing and updating Kanzi Engine plugins using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-and-updating-kanzi-engine-plugins-using-script).
       * Creating and updating of data sources. See [Creating and updating data sources using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-and-updating-data-sources-using-a-script).
       * Creating of nodes. See [Creating nodes using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-nodes-using-a-script).
       * Adding and removing of properties, and setting of property values. See [Editing properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#editing-properties-using-a-script).
       * Logging of invalid project items. See [Logging invalid project items using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#logging-invalid-project-items-using-a-script).
For the list of available commands, see [Kanzi Studio command reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html).
    3. Save and close the project.

```
# Save the project.
# The second parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio continues working in the directory where you
# opened the project.
# When you save the project to a different location, set the second parameter to false.
# For example,
# SaveProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyOtherProject\Tool_project\MyOtherProject.proj.kzm" false
SaveProject "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyProject\Tool_project\MyProject.proj.kzm" true

# Close Kanzi Studio.
# To close the project but continue using Kanzi Studio, use CloseProject.
ExitApplication

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. Open the command line interface, go to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin` directory, and run the `KanziStudio.exe` file with the `/Script` flag pointing to the script that you created in the previous step.
For example, on the command line interface, run

```
KanziStudio.exe /Script="C:\Users\username\Documents\MyScript.txt"

```
Copy to clipboard


## Exporting kzb files using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#exporting-kzb-files-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
A kzb file contains contents of a Kanzi Studio project. To run your Kanzi application, you must export the contents of the Kanzi Studio project of that application to a kzb file.
See [Using kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html).
To export kzb files using a script, use the [ExportBinary](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#exportbinary) command:

```
# Export the kzb file to the location set in the Project > Properties in the Binary Export Directory
# property.
# To export the kzb file to another location use:
# ExportBinary "Path\to\directory\MyProjectBinary.kzb"
ExportBinary

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/binary-export-directory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binary-export-directory.png) ![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
The `ExportBinary` command takes these optional parameters:
  * The first parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files. The default is true.
  * The second parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports kza file, which is the XML version of the kzb file. The default is false.


For example, to export both the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files, and the kza file:

```
# Export the theme and locale resources and the kza file.
ExportBinary true true

```
Copy to clipboard
## Building Kanzi applications for Android using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#building-k-applications-for-android-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To build Kanzi applications for Android using a script, use the [ExportApk](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#exportapk) command:

```
# Before you build an APK file, you can set whether to install the APK file to your
# Android device and launch the application. By default, |k| installs the APK file
# and launches the application.
# In My Android Configuration, disable the Install to Device property.
SetProperty "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" BuildConfigurationInstallToDevice false
# In My Android Configuration, disable the Launch Application property.
SetProperty "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" BuildConfigurationRunApplication false

# Build the APK file using the My Android Configuration build configuration.
# If the project contains images that use texture compression, the second
# parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio compresses these images.
ExportApk "/Resource Files/Build Configurations/My Android Configuration" true

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/library-my-android-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-my-android-configuration.png) ![../../_images/properties-my-android-configuration.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-my-android-configuration.png) ![../../_images/build-android-package.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/build-android-package.png)
## Importing and updating Kanzi Engine plugins using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-and-updating-kr-plugins-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Engine plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Engine. Kanzi Engine executes these plugins on target platforms.
See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html).
You can import and update Kanzi Engine plugins using a script:
  * [Importing a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-kanzi-engine-plugin-using-script)
  * [Updating a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-kanzi-engine-plugin-using-script)
  * [Updating all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project-or-solution-using-script)


### Importing a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-a-kr-plugin-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use a Kanzi Engine plugin in a Kanzi Studio project, you must import that Kanzi Engine plugin to your Kanzi Studio project.
To import a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script, use the [ImportEnginePlugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#importengineplugin) command:

```
# Import the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll.
# Kanzi Studio adds to the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins a reference to the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL that you import.
ImportEnginePlugin "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/import-kanzi-engine-plugin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-kanzi-engine-plugin.png) ![../../_images/mypluginproject-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mypluginproject-in-library.png)
### Updating a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-kr-plugin-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use in a Kanzi Studio project a different version of a Kanzi Engine plugin, you must update that Kanzi Engine plugin in your Kanzi Studio project.
To update a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script, use the [ImportEnginePlugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#importengineplugin) command:

```
# Update the XML_data_source Kanzi Engine plugin in the project.
# You leave the first parameter empty because you do not import a new plugin to the project.
ImportEnginePlugin "" "/Kanzi Engine Plugins/XML_data_source"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugin-metadata.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugin-metadata.png)
### Updating all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-kr-plugins-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use in a Kanzi Studio project a different version of a Kanzi Engine plugin, you must update that Kanzi Engine plugin in your Kanzi Studio project.
You can update all Kanzi Engine plugins in your Kanzi Studio project using a script. If your Kanzi Studio project contains project references, you can update all Kanzi Engine plugins in the solution which includes that project and all referenced projects. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
To update all Kanzi Engine plugins in a project or solution using a script, use the [UpdateProjectEnginePlugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updateprojectengineplugins) or [UpdateSolutionEnginePlugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatesolutionengineplugins) command:

```
# Update all the Kanzi Engine plugins in the project.
# To update the Kanzi Engine plugins in that project and all referenced projects use
# UpdateSolutionEnginePlugins.
UpdateProjectEnginePlugins

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-kanzi-engine-plugins-in-project.png)
## Creating and updating data sources using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-and-updating-data-sources-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Use data sources to separate the user interface from the application data and to remove the dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and the application code which define the Kanzi application.
See [Data sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html).
You can create and update data sources using a script:
  * [Creating a data source using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-a-data-source-using-a-script)
  * [Updating a data source using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-data-source-using-a-script)
  * [Updating all data sources in a project or solution using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-data-sources-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script)


### Creating a data source using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-a-data-source-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use a Kanzi Engine data source plugin in a Kanzi Studio project, you must create a data source in your Kanzi Studio project.
To create a data source using a script, first import a Kanzi Engine data source plugin, then create and update the data source:

```
# Import the Kanzi Engine data source plugin DLL MyDataSource\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Release_DLL\MyDataSource.dll.
# The MyDataSource plugin defines the CustomDataSourceType data source type.
# Kanzi Studio adds to the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins a reference to the Kanzi Engine data source plugin DLL that you import.
ImportEnginePlugin "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyDataSource\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Release_DLL\MyDataSource.dll"

# Create a data source named Cluster of the type CustomDataSourceType.
CreateDataSource "Cluster" "CustomDataSourceType"
# To create data objects from the Cluster data source, update the data source.
UpdateDataSourceContents "/Data Sources/Cluster/"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/mydatasource-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mydatasource-in-library.png) ![../../_images/mydatasource-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mydatasource-properties.png) ![../../_images/cluster-data-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cluster-data-source.png)
### Updating a data source using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-a-data-source-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
If the Kanzi Engine plugin that defines your data source does not update your data source, you can update the data source using a script.
To update a data source using a script, use the [UpdateDataSourceContents](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatedatasourcecontents) command:

```
# Update the Cluster data source in the project.
UpdateDataSourceContents "/Data Sources/Cluster/"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-data-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-data-source.png)
### Updating all data sources in a project or solution using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#updating-all-data-sources-in-a-project-or-solution-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
If the Kanzi Engine plugin that defines your data source does not update your data sources, you can update the data source using a script. If your Kanzi Studio project contains project references, you can update all data sources in the solution which includes that project and all referenced projects. See [Combining Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/using-assets-from-another-project.html).
To update all data sources in a project or solution using a script, use the [UpdateProjectDataSources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updateprojectdatasources) or [UpdateSolutionDataSources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#updatesolutiondatasources) command:

```
# Update all data sources in the project.
# To update the data sources in that project and all referenced projects use
# UpdateSolutionDataSources.
UpdateProjectDataSources

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/update-data-sources-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/update-data-sources-in-project.png)
## Creating nodes using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#creating-nodes-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
You can create nodes using a script. For example:
  * To create a Button 2D node, use the [CreateButton2D](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#createbutton2d) command:

```
# In the RootNode node, create a Button 2D node named My Button.
# The last parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio selects the node that you created.
CreateButton2D "/Screens/Screen/RootNode" "My Button" true

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/my-button-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-button-in-project.png)
  * To create a Grid List Box 3D node, use the [CreateComponentNode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#createcomponentnode) command:

```
# In the RootNode > Viewport 2D > Scene node, create a Grid List Box 3D node named My Grid List Box.
CreateComponentNode "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/Viewport 2D/Scene" "My Grid List Box" Kanzi.GridListBox3D

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/my-grid-list-box-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-grid-list-box-in-project.png)


## Editing properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#editing-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Properties provide the means to specify and examine the state, appearance, and behavior of nodes. For example, a property can define a color, indicate whether a button is pressed, or specify the alignment of an item.
See [Property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/property-types/property-types.html).
You can edit properties using a script:
  * [Adding properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#adding-properties-using-a-script)
  * [Removing properties using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#removing-properties-using-a-script)
  * [Setting property values using a script](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#setting-property-values-using-a-script)


### Adding properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#adding-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To add properties using a script, use the [AddProperty](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#addproperty) command.
For example, to add the Description property to the RootNode node:

```
# In the RootNode node, add the Description property.
AddProperty "MyProject/Screens/Screen/RootNode" Description

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/rootpage-description.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rootpage-description.png)
### Removing properties using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#removing-properties-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To remove properties using a script, use the [RemovePropertyFromItem](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#removepropertyfromitem) command.
For example, to remove the Background Brush property from the RootNode node:

```
# In the RootNode node, remove the Background Brush property.
# Use the Kanzi Engine property name which you see in Kanzi Studio when you hover your
# mouse pointer over the property name.
RemovePropertyFromItem "MyProject/Screens/Screen/RootNode" Node2D.BackgroundBrush

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/background-brush-kanzi-engine-name.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-kanzi-engine-name.png) ![../../_images/remove-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/remove-background-brush.png)
### Setting property values using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#setting-property-values-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
To set property values using a script, use the [SetProperty](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#setproperty) command.
For example:
  * To set the size of the Screen node to 1200 x 720 pixels:

```
# In the Screen node, set:
# - Metrics Type to Absolute
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" Window.MetricsType Absolute
# - Width to 1200
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" WindowAbsoluteWidth 1200
# - Height to 720
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" WindowAbsoluteHeight 720

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/metrics-type-absolute.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/metrics-type-absolute.png) ![../../_images/window-width-and-height-1200x720.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/window-width-and-height-1200x720.png)
  * To set the Text property of a Text Block node to one line of text:

```
# In the RootNode > My Text Block node, set the Text property to SERVICE VEHICLE SOON.
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/My Text Block" TextConcept.Text "SERVICE VEHICLE SOON"

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/text-single-line.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-single-line.png)
  * To set a property value that spans multiple lines, enclose the value between triple backticks:

```
# In the RootNode > My Text Block node, set the Text property to
# SERVICE
# VEHICLE
# SOON
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen/RootNode/My Text Block" TextConcept.Text ```SERVICE
VEHICLE
SOON```

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/text-multiline.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-multiline.png)


## Logging invalid project items using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#logging-invalid-project-items-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio marks invalid items in the Node Tree and Library with red type.
For example:
  * A node contains an invalid binding.
  * A resource uses a resource that does not exist or is missing a required property.
  * A material type has precision mismatches in its shaders.
  * A shader source file contains errors.

See [Finding invalid project items](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/finding-invalid-project-items.html).
To log invalid project items in your Kanzi Studio project using a script, use the [PrintDiagnosticReport](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#printdiagnosticreport) command:

```
# Print a list of invalid project items to the Log window and the KanziStudio.log file.
PrintDiagnosticReport MyProject

```

## Exporting kzb files using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#exporting-kzb-files-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
A kzb file contains contents of a Kanzi Studio project. To run your Kanzi application, you must export the contents of the Kanzi Studio project of that application to a kzb file.
See [Using kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html).
To export kzb files using a script, use the [ExportBinary](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#exportbinary) command:  
```
# Export the kzb file to the location set in the Project > Properties in the Binary Export Directory
# property.
# To export the kzb file to another location use:
# ExportBinary "Path\to\directory\MyProjectBinary.kzb"
ExportBinary

The `ExportBinary` command takes these optional parameters:
* The first parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files. The default is true.
* The second parameter sets whether Kanzi Studio exports kza file, which is the XML version of the kzb file. The default is false.  
For example, to export both the theme and locale resources to separate kzb files, and the kza file:  
```
# Export the theme and locale resources and the kza file.
ExportBinary true true

```

### Importing a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/automation/automation.html#importing-a-kr-plugin-using-a-script "Link to this heading")
When you want to use a Kanzi Engine plugin in a Kanzi Studio project, you must import that Kanzi Engine plugin to your Kanzi Studio project.
To import a Kanzi Engine plugin using a script, use the [ImportEnginePlugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html#importengineplugin) command:  
```
# Import the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll.
# Kanzi Studio adds to the Library > Kanzi Engine Plugins a reference to the Kanzi Engine plugin DLL that you import.
ImportEnginePlugin "C:\KanziWorkspace\Projects\MyPluginProject\Application\lib\Win64\GL_vs2022_Debug_DLL\MyPluginProject.dll"

# - Height to 720
SetProperty "/Screens/Screen" WindowAbsoluteHeight 720

It also notes that aliases can be used for accessing nodes and that kzb file URLs are used in code.

Use bookmarks to provide a quick way to access objects and resources in your Kanzi Studio project. To access resources and objects in your Kanzi application in code, use the kzb file URL.
Kanzi Studio stores bookmarks in the Library > Bookmarks.
To access nodes in your Kanzi Studio project or using the Kanzi API you can also use aliases. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
## Creating a bookmark from any item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#creating-a-bookmark-from-any-item "Link to this heading")
To create a bookmark from any item in Kanzi Studio, in the Node Tree, Nodes, or Library press `Alt` and right-click and select Bookmark.
Kanzi Studio creates a bookmark and sets its Target property to the item from which you created the bookmark.
## Accessing a bookmarked item[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#accessing-a-bookmarked-item "Link to this heading")
To access a bookmarked item, in the Library > Bookmarks double-click the bookmark of the item you want to access.
Kanzi Studio takes you to the bookmarked item.
## Changing the target of a bookmark[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#changing-the-target-of-a-bookmark "Link to this heading")
To change the item to which a bookmark points, in the Library select the bookmark, and in the Properties set the Target property to the item you want the bookmark to point to.
##  Bookmark property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html#bookmark-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for bookmarks, see [Bookmark](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/bookmark-reference.html).

small: This page introduces data sources in Kanzi, explaining how they separate the user interface from application data and remove dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and application code. It describes how to define the format and structure of a data source using a Kanzi Engine data source plugin, and how to bind property values to data from a source so that UI nodes and resources reflect data changes. Typical use cases include cluster and IVI systems binding to server-provided data such as speed, RPM, fuel, contacts, media, and navigation info. It also points to a tutorial and related documentation for defining, using, and implementing data sources in various languages.

Use data sources to separate the user interface from the application data and to remove the dependencies between a Kanzi Studio project and the application code which define the Kanzi application.
Kanzi allows you to define the format and structure of your data source by defining a Kanzi Engine data source plugin.
When you use a data source in a Kanzi application you bind the values of properties and property fields to data that comes from a data source. This binding establishes a connection between a node or a resource and the application data. When data in the data source changes, the nodes and resources which are bound to the data reflect the change in the data.
A typical use case is to bind the properties of nodes in your cluster or IVI system to data from a data source provided by a server to which your application connects. For example, your Kanzi application can use data sources to get data such as speed, RPM, and fuel information, address book entries, album and song information, navigation information, and so on.
Learn how to define and use data sources in your Kanzi applications by completing the data sources tutorial. See [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).

small:
To use data objects:
1. In the Node Tree select a node where you want to use a data source (or one of its parent nodes), in the Properties add the Data Context property, and set it to the data source from which you want to use the data.
For example, add and set the Data Context property to the RootNode node.
By setting the Data Context property you tell your application from which data source it receives data. When you set the Data Context property for a node, all its child nodes inherit the value of the Data Context property. If you want to use a different data context for one of the child nodes, add the Data Context property to that node and set it to the data context you want to use.
Tip
You can set the data context by dragging a data object from the Data Sources window and dropping it on a node in the Node Tree to which you want to assign that data context.

Unlike regular Lua scripts which are used in Execute Lua Action, your Lua data script must return a root `DataObject` which contains the data definition for your Lua data source.
Tip
You can define data objects in the Lua data script as global variables, so that other scripts can easily access and modify the data.
For example:

local rootDataObject = DataObject:create("cluster", {
speed = 100,
rpm = 2300,
notifications = {
{ notification = "Service Due"},
{ notification = "Oil Change Needed"},
{ notification = "Dirty Air Filter"},
},
})

#  Factory Content assets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#factory-content-assets "Link to this heading")

The Factory Content asset packages contain ready-made components and materials that you can use to create prototype projects faster.
Here you can find all the Factory Content assets:
  * 2D interactivity control components that you can use to make your application interactive. See [Interactivity control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Progress components that you can use to indicate that a task is in progress. See [Progress components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components).
  * List components that you can use to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists. See [List components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components).
  * Complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application. See [Complete user interface components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#materials).
  * Render Passes that you can use to add effects to your project. See [Render Passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes).


To use the Factory Content assets in your Kanzi Studio project, from the Asset Packages drag an asset to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
![../../_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-factory-content-selected.png)
## Interactivity control components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#interactivity-control-components "Link to this heading")
Use 2D interactivity control components to make your application interactive.
###  Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#button "Link to this heading")
Use the Button to create a button that receives user input.
![../../_images/button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Button, after you add the Button to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Label to set the text in the button.
  * Main Color to set the color of the button background.
  * Highlight Color to set the color of the button background when the user presses the button.
  * Border Color to set the color of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Border Thickness to set the width of the button border that is visible when the user presses the button.
  * Rounding Radius to set the roundness of the button corners.
For example, to make the button corners right-angle, set Rounding Radius to 0.

![../../_images/button-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-properties.png)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the button reacts to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
The Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Button when:
  * The user presses the button.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Button node, the button does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Checkbox[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#checkbox "Link to this heading")
Use the Checkbox to create a checkbox that receives user input.
![../../_images/checkbox.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/checkbox.gif)
The Checkbox uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the Checkbox when:
  * The user toggles the checkbox.
  * The value of the Enabled property changes.
When you disable the Enabled property in the Checkbox node, the checkbox does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)


###  Radio Buttons[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#radio-buttons "Link to this heading")
Use the Radio Buttons to create radio buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/radio-buttons.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/radio-buttons.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how radio buttons react to user input. See [Using the Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Slider[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#slider "Link to this heading")
Use the Slider to create a slider that receives user input.
![../../_images/slider1.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider1.gif)
To adjust the appearance and behavior of the Slider, after you add the Slider to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Maximum Value to set the highest value of the slider. The default value is 100.
  * Minimum Value to set the lowest value of the slider. The default value is 0.
  * Step Value to set the increment by which the knob moves on the rail. The default value is 1.
  * Value to set the initial position of the knob on the rail. You can use bindings to control another property with the position of the slider. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
  * Knob Style to set the shape of the knob to square or circle, or to not show the knob.
  * Knob Size to set the size of the knob.
  * Knob Color to set the color of the knob.
  * Rail Thickness to set the thickness of the rail.
  * Rail Rounded Ends to set whether to round the ends of the rail.
  * Rail Background Color to set the color of the rail from the knob until the end of the rail.
  * Rail Fill Color to set the color of the rail from the start of the rail until the knob.

![../../_images/slider-range-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-range-properties1.png) ![../../_images/slider-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-properties.png)
The Slider uses a state manager that sets the appearance and behavior of the slider when the value of the Enabled property changes. When you disable the Enabled property in the Slider node, the slider does not react to user input.
![../../_images/node-enabled-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-enabled-disabled.png)
###  Toggle Button[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#toggle-button "Link to this heading")
Use the Toggle Button to create a toggle button that receives user input.
![../../_images/toggle-button.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-button.gif)
The Toggle Button uses a state manager that sets the appearance of the Toggle Button when the user toggles it.
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the toggle button reacts to user input. See [Using the Toggle Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
## Progress components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-components "Link to this heading")
Use the progress components to show that a task is in progress.
###  Processing Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#processing-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Processing Indicator to show that the application is processing a task.
![../../_images/processing-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator.gif)
To adjust the appearance of the Processing Indicator, after you add the Processing Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Color to set the color of the processing indicator.
  * Masked to set whether to mask the processing indicator with the texture that you set using the Masking Texture property.
  * Masking Texture to a texture to use to mask the processing indicator.
In the masking texture:
    * Black pixels form the mask that hides areas of the processing indicator.
    * White pixels form the gaps in the mask that show areas of the processing indicator.
By default the Processing Indicator is masked by a texture that shows a ring of circles.
  * Offset to set the rotation angle of the processing indicator.
  * Step Count to set the number of segments in the processing indicator.

![../../_images/processing-indicator-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-properties.png)
###  Progress Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Bar to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Bar, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress bar, in the Properties set the value of the Smoothing property.
![../../_images/progress-bar-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-bar-properties.png)
###  Progress Indicator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#progress-indicator "Link to this heading")
Use the Progress Indicator to show that a task is in progress, expressed both visually and as a percentage.
![../../_images/progress-indicator.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator.gif)
To set the value of the Progress Indicator, in the Properties set the value of the Progress property. You can use bindings to control the Progress property. See [Using bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html).
To adjust the appearance of the Progress Indicator, after you add the Progress Indicator to your project, in the Properties set:
  * Brush Color to set the color of the progress indicator ring.
  * Progress Smoothness to set the length of the gradient in the end of the progress indicator.
  * Ring Smoothness to set the edge smoothness of the progress indicator ring.
  * Ring Thickness to set the width of the progress indicator ring.

![../../_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-brush-color.png) ![../../_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/progress-indicator-properties1.png)
## List components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#list-components "Link to this heading")
Use the list components to present collections of items arranged in scrollable lists.
Each list component uses a List Box node to arrange its items. See [List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html).
Use a data source to display your own data in a list component. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html), and [Tutorial: Get application data from a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html).
###  Contact List[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#contact-list "Link to this heading")
Use the Contact List to create a contact list that shows the name, profile picture, and phone number for each contact.
![../../_images/contact-list.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contact-list.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Contact List, in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
###  Cover Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#cover-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Cover Flow to present album covers.
![../../_images/cover-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cover-flow.gif)
To set the content and behavior of the Cover Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Cover Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
###  Poster Flow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#poster-flow "Link to this heading")
Use the Poster Flow to present media posters.
![../../_images/poster-flow.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow.gif)
To adjust the roundness of poster corners, in the Prefabs select the Poster prefab and in the Properties set the Rounding Radius property.
![../../_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/poster-flow-rounding-radius.png)
To set the content and behavior of the Poster Flow, in the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Poster Flow > Scene> Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Items Source to provide a data source for the list items.
  * Selection Behavior to set whether the list box brings an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item.

![../../_images/items-source-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/items-source-property.png) ![../../_images/selection-behavior-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior-property.png)
## Complete user interface components[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#complete-user-interface-components "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes complete user interface components that you can use to add functionality to your application.
###  Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model.
![../../_images/car-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window. See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
###  Music Player[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#music-player "Link to this heading")
Use the Music Player to create a music player with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/music-player.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/music-player.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Music Player buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Navigation Bar[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#navigation-bar "Link to this heading")
Use the Navigation Bar to create a navigation bar with toggle buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/navigation-bar.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-bar.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Navigation Bar buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html)
###  Notification Popup[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#notification-popup "Link to this heading")
Use the Notification Popup to create a notification dialog with buttons that receive user input.
![../../_images/notification-popup.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-popup.gif)
In the Node Components use triggers and actions to set how the Notification Popup buttons react to user input. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).
###  Traditional Gauges[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#traditional-gauges "Link to this heading")
Use the Traditional Gauges to create a car cluster with speed, RPM, fuel, and temperature gauges.
![../../_images/traditional-gauges.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/traditional-gauges.gif)
To control the visibility of the speed and RPM gauges, in the Properties add and set the Gauge State property.
To move the indicators, in the Properties add and set:
  * Fuel to move the fuel indicator.
  * RPM to move the RPM indicator.
  * Speed to move the speed indicator.
  * Temperature to move the temperature indicator.

![../../_images/gauges-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/gauges-properties.png)
## Materials[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#materials "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project.
![../../_images/aluminium.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/aluminium.png)
Aluminium Material
Uses normal map textures.
![../../_images/car-paint-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-paint-material.png)
Car Paint Material
![../../_images/carbon-fiber-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carbon-fiber-material.png)
Carbon Fiber Material
Uses normal map textures.
![../../_images/chrome-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/chrome-material.png)
Chrome Material
![../../_images/glass-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/glass-material.png)
Glass Material
![../../_images/leather-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/leather-material.png)
Leather Material

## Render Passes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#render-passes "Link to this heading")
Factory Content includes render passes that you can use to add effects to your project.
###  Skybox render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html#skybox-render-pass "Link to this heading")
Use the Skybox render pass to draw a Cubemap as a background into your Scene.
![../../_images/skybox-asset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-asset.gif)
To set up the Skybox render pass
  * In Asset Packages > Factory Content, right-click Skybox and select Import to bring the package as a prefab in to the Library > Render Pass Prefabs folder.
  * If you do not have a custom Render Pass Prefab selected in your Viewport 2D, in Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, right-click and Create > Default render pass. In the Properties of your Viewport 2D, set the Default render pass as the value of the Render Pass Prefab property.
  * In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs, drag the Skybox render pass from its root node under the Draw Objects Opaque node of the Render Pass Prefab assigned to the target Viewport 2D.
  * To adjust the Skybox background, select and adjust the properties on the Skybox Render Pass View in the previous step.
    * To adjust the color of the background, adjust the CubemapColor property.
    * To select the background cubemap texture, use the TextureCube property.
    * To override the tracking camera, use the Override Camera property.
    * To adjust the orientation of the background, use the Skybox Orientation property.

![../../_images/skybox-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/skybox-properties.png)

Use triggers and actions to create interactions based on user input.
A trigger defines a condition and an action defines what the trigger does when that condition is met. For example, to print a message to the Log window when a node is attached to the node tree, add the On Attached trigger to that node and add the Write Log action to that trigger.
Kanzi Studio has a range of actions which you can add to a trigger. For example, you can add an action to print to the Log window (Write Log), set a property to a certain value (Set Property), activate an a Activity node (Activate Activity), or change application theme (Activate Theme).

## Trigger messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#trigger-messages "Link to this heading")
When a trigger intercepts a message that originates from an action you can set what the trigger does with the message. You can:
* Intercept the message, act on it, and let it continue traveling up or down the project tree.
* Intercept the message, act on it, and handle it. When a trigger handles a message it consumes it so that the message stops at the trigger that handles it and no other node can intercept it.

## Trigger messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#trigger-messages "Link to this heading")
When a trigger intercepts a message that originates from an action you can set what the trigger does with the message. You can:
* Intercept the message, act on it, and let it continue traveling up or down the project tree.
* Intercept the message, act on it, and handle it. When a trigger handles a message it consumes it so that the message stops at the trigger that handles it and no other node can intercept it.

small: With a trigger you can intercept a message either at the node where the message originates, or in a trigger in any of its ancestor or descendant nodes. You can intercept many different message types in the same node. When a message travels up the project tree, the message bubbles. When a message travels down the project tree, the message tunnels. You can set in the action that creates the message whether the message bubbles, tunnels, or both bubbles and tunnels.

metadata.big: With a trigger you can intercept a message either at the node where the message originates, or in a trigger in any of its ancestor or descendant nodes. You can intercept many different message types in the same node. When a message travels up the project tree, the message bubbles. When a message travels down the project tree, the message tunnels. You can set in the action that creates the message whether the message bubbles, tunnels, or both bubbles and tunnels.

small:
For example, if the action creates a bubbling message, after an action generates a message, the message bubbles from the node that receives the input to its parent node, then to the parent of the parent, and so on until a trigger intercepts the message. If the trigger also handles the message, the message stops bubbling (traveling up the project tree). If none of the ancestors handle the message, the message travels all the way to the root node of the project.
By default all triggers handle their own messages. You can control the handling of trigger messages by setting the Set Message Handled property in the trigger.

## Data Triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#data-triggers "Link to this heading")
Use a Data Trigger to:
* Apply a value to a property with an Apply Property Action
* Activate an Activity with an Apply Activation Action. See [Activating Activities with an Apply Activation Action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/pah.html#pah-apply-activation-action) and [Tutorial: Control application UI](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-trigger/data-trigger.html).  
A Data Trigger keeps the change on a node applied for as long as the condition expression in that Data Trigger is met. When the condition in that Data Trigger is no longer met, Kanzi reverts the changes that it applied using that Data Trigger.

Use a Data Trigger to:
* Apply a value to a property with an Apply Property Action
* Activate an Activity with an Apply Activation Action. See [Activating Activities with an Apply Activation Action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/pah.html#pah-apply-activation-action) and [Tutorial: Control application UI](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-trigger/data-trigger.html).  
A Data Trigger keeps the change on a node applied for as long as the condition expression in that Data Trigger is met. When the condition in that Data Trigger is no longer met, Kanzi reverts the changes that it applied using that Data Trigger.

small:
You set the condition in a Data Trigger in the form of a binding expression that evaluates to either `True` or `False`. In the condition you can use as an input either a property or a data source.
For example, you can use a Data Trigger to control the logic and activation state of Activities in an Activity Host.
Apply Activation Action and Apply Property Action actions have higher priority than any other actions. For example, if you use an Apply Activation Action that sets the Active Index property and a Set Property action that sets that same property to a different value, the effect of the Set Property action becomes visible only after Kanzi unapplies the Apply Activation Action.

## Adding a trigger[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-a-trigger "Link to this heading")
The most common place to add a triggers is in the node that uses the trigger, but you can add a trigger to any node.
To add a trigger:
1. In the Node Tree create or select a node to which you want to add a trigger.
For example, create a Button 2D node. When you create the Button 2D node it already has a Button: Click trigger.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png)
2. In the Node Components right-click Triggers and select a trigger that intercepts the type of message that you want to intercept. See [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).

## Setting the handling of trigger messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#setting-the-handling-of-trigger-messages "Link to this heading")
When a trigger handles a message it consumes it so that the message stops at the trigger that handles it and no other node can intercept it. See [Creating custom messages in Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#creating-custom-messages).
To set the handling of trigger messages, in the Node Components > Triggers, in the trigger for which you want to set message handling, set:
Set Message Handled property:
* When you enable the Set Message Handled property, this trigger intercepts and handles the message. The message stops here, and does not continue neither bubbling nor tunneling in the project tree.

small:
* When you disable the Set Message Handled property, this trigger intercepts the message, but the message continues bubbling or tunneling in the project tree.  
Routing Mode property:
* Bubbling to intercept only bubbling messages.
* Tunneling to intercept only tunneling messages.
* Tunneling and bubbling to intercept tunneling and bubbling messages.  
Message Source property:
* To intercept messages from a specific target item, do one of the following:
* Select the item from the dropdown menu.
* Select <Relative> and set the path to the item:
* Separate node names with `/` to build the path.
* Use `.` to access the current item.
* Use `..` to access the parent item of the current item.
* Use `#` to access a node using an alias in the resource dictionary of the current node. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).

### Creating a condition using a value from a property[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-property "Link to this heading")
You can define a trigger condition to set off a trigger when a property that you select gets a value you set in that condition. For example, you can create a condition that allows the user to scroll a Scroll View node only when a specific Page node is active.
To create a condition using a value from a property:
1. In the Node Tree select or create a node with a trigger to which you want to add a condition, in the Node Components in that trigger right-click Conditions, and select Trigger Condition. See [Adding a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-a-trigger).

small:
For example, create a Scroll View 2D node with a Scroll View: Scrolled trigger, in that trigger right-click Conditions, and select Trigger Condition. See [Using the Scroll View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html).
![../../_images/create-scroll-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-scroll-view.png) ![../../_images/scrolled-trigger-add-trigger-condition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scrolled-trigger-add-trigger-condition.png)
2. In the trigger condition that you created set the condition that must be met for the trigger to set off.
You create a trigger condition by comparing a value that you define in the A section to the value that you define in the B section using an operator that you set with the Operation property.
In the trigger condition set:

small:
In the trigger condition set:
* In the A section define the property type and value that you want to use for the condition. To use a value from a property, set:
* Type of A to Property
* Item to the node whose property you want to use for the condition
For example, set it to a Page node.
* Property to the property type that you want to use for the condition
For example, set it to the Activation State property of the Page node you selected in the Item property.
Use the Activation State property to find out whether a Page or Page Host node is active.
![../../_images/value-a.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/value-a.png)
* Operation to the operator that you want to use to compare the value that you defined in the A section to the value that you define in the B section.

small: This page explains filters in Kanzi, which collect and reorganize 3D nodes for rendering. Filters are used in render passes to determine which nodes to render, either via Object Source property in Draw Objects render passes or via Filter property in Node List render passes. Available filters include Contains Property Filter, Object Type Filter, Property Is Equal Filter, Sorting Filter, and Tag Filter. The page also mentions using filters in the API via the FilterObjectSource class and provides links to related tutorials and documentation.

# Filters[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html#filters "Link to this heading")

Filters collect and reorganize 3D nodes in your Kanzi project. You can use filters to determine which 3D nodes to render in different render passes.
After you set one or more filters or object sources, a filter collects and outputs a set of 3D nodes that match the requirements you define in that filter.
Use filters to adjust the rendering for the whole or parts of your Kanzi application. To use a filter, either:
  * In a Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass set the Object Source property so that the render pass renders only those nodes that the filter passes to the render pass.
  * In a Node List render pass set the Filter property so that the Node List render pass holds only those nodes that the filter passes to that Node List render pass.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.


See [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html).
For example, you can use filters to:
  * Create reflections for nodes. See [Tutorial: Create reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/reflections/reflections.html).
  * Apply a stencil to 3D content. See [Tutorial: Apply a stencil to 3D content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/stencil/stencil.html).
  * Distribute rendering across several frames. See [Tutorial: Progressive rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/progressive-rendering/progressive-rendering.html).
  * Render only transparent nodes. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).


These filters are available in Kanzi Studio in the Library > Rendering > Object Sources:
  * Contains Property Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property.
See [Using the Contains Property Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-contains-property-filters.html).
  * Object Type Filter collects 3D nodes based on their type. See [Using the Object Type Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-object-type-filters.html).
  * Property Is Equal Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property the value of which matches a specific value.
See [Using the Property Is Equal Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-property-is-equal-filters.html).
  * Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
See [Using the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html).
  * Tag Filter collects 3D nodes that have a specific tag assigned.
See [Using the Tag Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-tag-filters.html).

small:
* Property Type to the property for which you want to filter your nodes.
* Operation to either:
* Include to collect the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
* Exclude to leave out the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
![../../_images/contains-property-filter-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/contains-property-filter-properties.png)
3. To take the Contains Property Filter into use, either:
* In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.

* In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.

small:
* In the Node List render pass that you use to hold the nodes that you want to render using other render passes, set the Filter property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.
For example:
1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Group render pass and inside it create:
* Clear render pass
* Gather Lights render pass and inside it a Draw Objects render pass
![../../_images/render-passes-for-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-for-filters.png)

Property Is Equal Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property the value of which matches a specific value.
To use the Property Is Equal Filter:
1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Rendering > Object Sources and select Property Is Equal Filter.
![../../_images/create-property-is-equal-filter.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-property-is-equal-filter.png)
2. In the Properties set:
* Source to the source from where you want to collect nodes for filtering. For example, to apply your filter to all nodes in your project, select Root Object Source. You can select the output of another filter as the source from where you collect nodes for filtering.

small:
* Property Type to the property for which you want to filter your nodes.
* Operation to either:
* Include to collect the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
* Exclude to leave out the nodes that contain the property you set in the Property Type property.
* Depending on the property you selected in the Property Type, set the value of the property you want the Property Is Equal Filter to collect.
![../../_images/property-is-equal-filter-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/property-is-equal-filter-properties.png)
3. To take the Property Is Equal Filter into use, either:
* In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.

3. To take the Property Is Equal Filter into use, either:
* In the Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass that you use to render the 3D nodes to which you want to apply the filter, set the Object Source property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.

small:
* In the Node List render pass that you use to hold the nodes that you want to render using other render passes, set the Filter property to the filter or to an object source that collects the filter.
Use a Node List render pass when you want to filter anything but the 3D nodes that you want to render, such as Light nodes. Draw Objects render pass, Draw Objects With Material render pass, and Gather Lights render passes can use the result node list of the same Node List render pass.
For example:
1. In the Library > Rendering > Render Pass Prefabs create a Group render pass and inside it create:
* Clear render pass
* Gather Lights render pass and inside it a Draw Objects render pass
![../../_images/render-passes-for-filters.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-passes-for-filters.png)

Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
For example, use sorting filters to optimize the performance of your Kanzi application:
* **Preventing overdraw.**
Excessive overdraw can decrease performance on the GPU in the form of increased fill-rate. See [Preventing overdraw with the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/preventing-overdraw-with-sorting-filters.html).
* **Rendering transparent objects.**

Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
For example, use sorting filters to optimize the performance of your Kanzi application:
* **Preventing overdraw.**

* **Rendering transparent objects.**

small:
* **Rendering transparent objects.**
Because visualization of transparent nodes relies on having proper data behind them, in order to solve the blending equations properly, to correctly render transparent nodes, you must render them from back to front. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).
* **Reducing shader switches.**
If nodes are presented in an order that requires excessive switching between shader programs, the rendering can slow down. See [Reducing shader switches](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/reducing-shader-switches.html).  
To use the Sorting Filter:
1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Rendering > Object Sources and select Sorting Filter.

small:
Overdraw issues occur when one node is first drawn to an area of pixels in the back buffer, after which another node is presented that occludes the first node, and the same pixels are filled again. Excessive overdraw can decrease performance on the GPU in the form of increased fill-rate. If you order nodes so that the occluding node is drawn first, the occluded pixels do not have to be rendered again because of the depth buffering.
See [Preventing overdraw with the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/preventing-overdraw-with-sorting-filters.html).
* Material type to group the nodes by their material type.

small: This page introduces the focus system in Kanzi, explaining how key focus forwards hardware key messages to UI elements. It defines core concepts such as focusable nodes, key focus node, focus chain, focus order, and focus scopes. It describes focus scope types (focus group, focus fence, modal/modeless overlays, auto-closing variants) and the focus state property values (No Focus, Logical Focus, Key Focus). It also provides links to related guides on using focus and handling user input.

Key focus forwards hardware key messages to the correct user interface element in your application. For example, the user can press the arrow keys on the keyboard to move a slider or press the `Enter` key to click a button.
Kanzi organizes nodes in focus scopes. Focus scopes are nodes which assist in focus chain navigation handling. They group the child nodes and drive the focus navigation within that group. They also act like a focus proxy, forwarding the focus to one of their focusable child nodes. When you move the focus away from a focus scope, that scope remembers the last-focused child node.
These are the main concepts behind how focus works in Kanzi:
  * **Focusable node** is a node that has the Focusable property enabled. A focusable node can receive key input.
  * **Key focus node** is the node that currently receives key input, and has the read-only Focused property enabled. A Kanzi application can have only one key focus node at a time.
  * **Focus chain** is a sequence of nodes which defines the order in which Kanzi sets key focus to those nodes. Kanzi includes in the focus chain all focusable nodes in your project.
[![../../_images/focus-chain.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-chain.svg)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-chain.svg)
  * **Focus order** defines the position of a node in the focus chain based on the position of the node in the node tree or the value of its Focus Order property.
[![../../_images/focus-order.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-order.svg)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-order.svg)
  * **Focus scope** is a node that helps navigation handling in a focus chain. You can set a node to be a focus scope to forward the focus from that node to a child node.
[![../../_images/focus-scope.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-scope.svg)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/focus-scope.svg)
These are the focus scope types in Kanzi:
    * **Focus group** is a focus scope which forms a group of focusable nodes. When a focus group node receives focus, Kanzi forwards the focus to the focus node of that focus scope.
You can move focus within the boundaries of a focus group and outside of a focus group.
    * **Focus fence** is a focus scope that keeps the focus chain navigation inside the scope and does not allow the focus chain navigation to enter or leave that scope. A focus fence allows the user to navigate the content within the scope boundaries.
    * These overlay-type focus scopes:
      * **Modal overlay** blocks the key and touch input that originates from outside its boundaries and keeps the focus navigation within the overlay boundaries, just like a focus fence. Every Kanzi application has at least one modal overlay: the Screen node.
      * **Auto-closing modal overlay** is similar to modal overlay, except that when the overlay is an Activity in a Parallel Activity Host, the Parallel Activity Host deactivates that Activity when user input originates from outside the boundaries of that Activity.
      * **Modeless overlay** propagates the key and touch input that originates from outside its boundaries, but keeps the focus navigation within the focus scope boundaries, just like a modal overlay.
      * **Auto-closing modeless overlay** is similar to modeless overlay, except that when the overlay is an Activity in a Parallel Activity Host, the Parallel Activity Host deactivates that Activity when user input originates from outside the boundaries of that Activity.
  * **Focus state** reports the focus state of a node or nodes in a focus scope. These are the available values for the Focus State property:  
| Enumeration value  | Enumeration key  | Meaning for a focusable node  | Meaning for a focus scope  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| No Focus  | 0  | The node does not have focus.  | None of the nodes in the focus scope have focus.  |  
| Logical Focus  | 1  | The node is the logical focus node of an overlay-type focus scope. The logical focus node was the key focus node before the overlay lost the focus. When the overlay regains the focus, the logical focus node becomes the key focus node.  | A node in the focus scope is the logical focus node of the overlay to which the scope belongs.  |  
| Key Focus  | 2  | The node is the key focus node of the application.  | A node in the focus scope is the key focus node of the application.  |  


To learn more about creating focus navigation for your application, see [Using focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/setting-focus.html).

## Default keyboard navigation keys[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/setting-focus.html#default-keyboard-navigation-keys "Link to this heading")
These are the default keyboard keys you can use to move focus in your application:
* Navigate in the forward direction by pressing the `Tab` key and in the backward direction by pressing the `BackTab` key or `Shift` `Tab` keys.
* The Button nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. When a Button node has focus, to press that button, you can use the default keyboard keys `Space`, `Enter`, and `Enter` on the numeric pad.
* The Toggle Button nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. When a Toggle Button node has focus, to press that button, you can use the default keyboard keys `Space`, `Enter`, and `Enter` on the numeric pad.

* `End` to move the slider knob to the end of the rail
* `←` and `→` to move the knob of a horizontal slider
